description: The lake requires a moderate 3-5km out and back hike to access. The hike is mostly along an old deactivated road until the last portion you follow a 250m trail to the north to reach the lake. Look for a sign on a birch tree saying Leviathan Lake. The quiet lake has distant mountain views and many dragonflies and lilly pads.
directions:
This trail can be accessed by boat or by 4x4 capable vehicles along the Powder-Clute FSR.

Boat Access: The trailhead is located on the east side of Kootenay Lake, south of Campbell Bay. Coordinates: 49.56'16.12"N / 116.51'37.28"W. Hike up the deactivated road for 2.2km until you reach the lake.

4x4 Access: From Riondel head North on Eastman Ave and then continue onto Riondel North Rd. Follow the road to the end where you reach Powder Creek FSR. You will need a high clearance 4x4 vehicle for this portion of road. Follow the Powder Creek FSR, which will turn into the Powder-Clute FSR (the main FSR-keeping left at the forks) for 21.5 km until you see a deactivated road on your right. Do not drive down this section of road. Park your vehicle in the pull out off the FSR and hike 1.7km to the lake.
title: Laviathon Trail
